SUMMARY: Stop the architecture-factor line added in c754e8b to factor.py from matching every arch in a multiline factor-conditional value, which leaves an unbalanced quote that breaks `{[tox]arch}` for `py39-x86_64` on an arm64 host.

FILES: tests/config/loader/ini/test_factor.py : add a regression test from the ticket's ini; add or update a test so implicit arch matching still works when the env name has no arch factor
FUNCTIONS: filter_for_env, expand_factors
APPROACH: Likely mechanism: the added line also puts an arch factor in `current` that the env name does not state (probably the host or interpreter machine, arm64 here). For `py39-x86_64`, both the `x86_64:` and `arm64:` lines of `[tox]arch` then match, so the value becomes "x86_64\narm64". That newline splits the command and leaves the quote unbalanced, giving `"print('…x86_64`. Read c754e8b and its tests to see what the add is for, confirm this mechanism, then keep that use case working. Add the implicit factor only when the env name contains no explicit arch-like factor, or only for the pairs that need it, so `filter_for_env` returns exactly one line per env in the regression case (both env names, run on an arm64 or x86_64 host).
RISKS: The arch value may come from `platform.machine()` or the interpreter, so tests must pin or mock it to be reproducible across CI hosts; the existing ISA-factor tests that broke when the reporter removed the line must still pass. M-level design choice (what counts as an explicit arch factor), so use the sonnet/medium default.

TICKET: T1
SUMMARY: Stop `filter_for_env` from auto-adding the host platform and machine-arch factors when the env name already names a different platform or arch. Today `py39-x86_64` on an arm64 Mac matches both `x86_64:` and `arm64:` lines, so `{[tox]arch}` expands to two lines and breaks the command.
FILES: src/tox/config/loader/ini/factor.py : put host-factor injection behind a helper; skip `sys.platform` / `sysconfig` arch when the env's explicit factors already contain a known platform / arch name
FILES: src/tox/config/loader/toml/_replace.py : make `Unroll._extract_factors` reuse the same helper so INI and TOML factor semantics stay identical
FILES: tests/config/loader/ini/test_factor.py : add a regression test for the ticket's ini and an arch-only env; monkeypatch `sysconfig.get_platform` to `macosx-11.0-arm64` and `sys.platform` to `darwin`
FILES: docs/changelog/3902.bugfix.rst (new) : one-line changelog fragment (the pre-commit hook enforces this name pattern)
FUNCTIONS: filter_for_env, _host_factors (new), Unroll._extract_factors
APPROACH: Root cause, traced in the code: `filter_for_env` builds `current` from the env-name factors plus `sys.platform` plus the last segment of `sysconfig.get_platform()` (`arm64` on a Mac). Env `py39-x86_64` then satisfies both `x86_64: x86_64` and `arm64: arm64`. The value becomes `x86_64\narm64`, gets substituted mid-command, and `StrConvert.to_list` splits the command at that newline. Fix: add a helper `_host_factors(explicit: set[str]) -> set[str]` with module-level frozensets of known arch names (`x86_64`, `amd64`, `arm64`, `aarch64`, `i386`, `i686`, `x86`, `win32`, `armv7l`, `ppc64le`, `s390x`, `riscv64`, `universal2`) and platform names (`linux`, `darwin`, `win32`, `cygwin`, `freebsd`, …). The helper returns the host platform only if `explicit` has no known platform name, and the host arch only if `explicit` has no known arch name. Keep host factors when `name is None` or the env name has no such factor, so existing tests for implicit platform/arch matching still pass. Run the full `tests/config` suite.
RISKS: Any hard-coded list of arch/platform names is incomplete. Keep the lists in one place so they are easy to extend, and do not drop host injection altogether, because the tests the reporter mentioned depend on it. Also check whether `tox_env/python/api.py` or the env_select factor validation (`_DYNAMIC_ENV_FACTORS`, `_combinable_factors`) relies on arch factors always being present.

I've read the factor code and written the brief below. The cause: since 4.46.0, tox adds the host CPU architecture as an implicit factor. On an Apple Silicon Mac, `py39-x86_64` therefore carries both `x86_64` and `arm64`. Both lines of `arch` match, the substituted value spans two lines, and the command gets cut in half. The TOML loader has the same code, so the fix should cover both.

TICKET: T1
SUMMARY: The host CPU architecture that tox adds as an implicit factor (since 4.46.0) wrongly matches alongside an architecture already in the env name (e.g. `arm64` added to `py39-x86_64` on Apple Silicon), so both lines of a multiline factor value match and the command breaks; the env-name architecture must take precedence.
